## `/usr/libexec/nebulaos/nebulaos-boot-display`

Called by: `docs/reference/RUNTIME-HELPERS.md`, `scripts/build/06-verify.sh`, `etc/init.d/S01persistent-datastore`, `etc/init.d/S01splash`, `tests/nebulaos-boot-display-tests.sh`, `tools/hardware/nebulaos_capture.py`, ...and 2 more.

nebulaos-boot-display - userspace boot display (GUI/service readiness mission, 2026-10-09).
Shell only: Python never runs on the boot path.

```
draw     S01persistent-datastore, right after /usr/data is mounted: show
the configured mode as early as possible (G3)
boot     S01splash: show it unless "draw" already did, then schedule the
late re-render
```

The "console" mode (a text boot log on the LCD) was removed (D10, 2026-10-11): once the
framebuffer console had taken over the display, GuppyScreen's start deadlocked in the kernel. A
saved "console" shows the logo. The kernel no longer has a framebuffer console at all.

Every step is best effort and bounded; any doubt means "do nothing" and the screen stays as the
boot loader left it. The backlight is never touched here (the display-qualification/backlight
layer owns it).

## `/usr/libexec/nebulaos/nebulaos-busy`

Called by: `artifacts/buildroot-halley5-v30-image/README.md`, `artifacts/buildroot-halley5-v30-image/buildroot.config`, `br2-external/board/nebulaos-x2000/.gitignore`, `br2-external/configs/nebulaos_x2000_defconfig`, `docs/NEBULAOS_CORE_PUBLIC_API.md`, `docs/NEBULAOS_MEMORY_RESILIENCE.md`, ...and 20 more.

nebulaos-busy - the G91 shared busy check for shell callers and SSH.

nebulaos-busy [--profile PROFILE] [--holder TOKEN] [--refuse] nebulaos-busy [--profile PROFILE]
--lock NAME --exec CMD [ARG...]

PROFILE: request (default) point_of_no_return git restart recovery screen.

Plain: prints BUSY=<reason> (PRINTING PAUSED ACTIVE CALIBRATING UPDATING LOW_MEMORY UNKNOWN) or
BUSY=no, then MESSAGE=<text> and KLIPPY=<state>. exit 0 = not busy (go ahead), 1 = busy, 64 =
usage.

--refuse (G91 step 6, for the CLI tools): prints nothing on stdout; busy -> "NebulaOS refused:
<message> (<REASON>)" on stderr and exit 3 (the osconfig refusal code), not busy -> exit 0.

--lock NAME --exec CMD...: takes the maintenance lock (token NAME-<pid>), runs the check with
that token excluded, and on "not busy" execs CMD with the lock still held (the fd is inherited;
it dies with CMD) and NEBULAOS_MAINTENANCE_HOLDER=<token> in its environment, so CMD can re-
check at its own point of no return (--holder "$NEBULAOS_MAINTENANCE_HOLDER"). Another holder
-> UPDATING. Refusals as --refuse (exit 3, nothing run). nebulaos-mcu, nebulaos-recover and
flash-spare-slot.sh re-exec themselves through this unless --force.

The same check as nebulaos_osconfig.common.busy_state (the [nebulaos] component and the
osconfig verbs); /etc/nebulaos-busy.sh is the fast shell variant of the restart/recovery/screen
profiles (supervisorctl shim, update supervisor).

## `/usr/libexec/nebulaos/nebulaos-clean-reset`

Called by: `docs/reference/OSCONFIG.md`, `docs/reference/RUNTIME-HELPERS.md`, `scripts/build/06-verify.sh`, `etc/init.d/S01persistent-datastore`, `usr/lib/nebulaos/python/nebulaos_osconfig/cleanup.py`, `usr/lib/nebulaos/python/nebulaos_osconfig/system.py`, ...and 5 more.

nebulaos-clean-reset - the boot half of the clean NebulaOS reset (S2, 2026-10-11). Sourced by
S01persistent-datastore right after /usr/data is mounted and before anything uses
/usr/data/nebulaos.

When the flag written by `nebulaos-osconfig system clean-reset` is present, the whole NebulaOS
namespace is removed: printer.cfg and calibration, Moonraker's database and history, Wi-Fi
networks, network settings, the root password, the boot screen, GuppyScreen's settings. The
rest of the boot then seeds everything from this image, exactly as on a new printer.

Kept: the device's identity - the Wi-Fi MAC seed (so the router keeps the same address) and the
SSH host keys (so SSH clients and the Hardware Agent still recognise the printer, G1) - and
everything outside /usr/data/nebulaos: the other boot slot's files and the shared G-code folder
(/usr/data/printer_data/gcodes).

Left behind for afterwards (G2, G28): a line in /usr/data/.nebulaos-clean-reset.log (outside
the wiped folder, so the reset itself stays on record) and the marker
/usr/data/nebulaos/.after-clean-reset, which makes the screen say once that Wi-Fi has to be
connected again (cleared by system ack-clean-reset).

Crash-safe: the namespace is first renamed (one atomic step), then deleted; a power cut in
between leaves a .nebulaos-wiping-* directory that the next boot deletes. The flag is removed
only after the rename, so an interrupted reset repeats harmlessly. Nothing happens on a read-
only /usr/data.
